propositions: When a compaction sweep holds the store write lock, a blocked session sees only a bare pid in the LockTimeout message and cannot determine whether interrupting the holder is safe.
The sweep operation is interruptible and safe to terminate, but this guarantee is not communicated to operators, who default to waiting rather than acting.
The holder's identity and interruptibility status are already known to the code but do not reach the timeout error message.
An ambient operation-label mechanism using contextvars can attach metadata to lock acquisitions without modifying per-ticket acquisition call sites.
The lock stamp format supports forward-compatible key=value fields that can name the holder's operation and reach the error message.
Operators need both the label identifying the holder as a compaction sweep and explicit remedy text stating that interrupting it loses no data.
